result.title: Sparsity Should Be ALLOTted by Output: Training-Free Allocation of Block-Sparse Attention for Video Diffusion Transformers
result.summary: Full 3D attention is costly in video Diffusion Transformers. Block-sparse attention reduces this cost by computing only selected attention blocks. However, existing methods either overlook the potential to optimize sparsity allocation or rely on heuristic rules or local metrics to guide it. In this work, we observe that sparsifying attention in different layers and at different denoising steps affects final-video fidelity to substantially different degrees. Yet the identities of the most sensitive layer-step pairs remain nearly unchanged across inputs. Building on these findings, we propose Allocating Layer-step Latency by Output Tests (ALLOT), a training-free sparsity allocation method. Treating each layer-step pair as a cell, ALLOT estimates each cell's contribution to final-video error through (i) cell probing and (ii) trajectory calibration, then jointly optimizes cell densities under a measured-latency budget. It preserves existing selection strategies and kernels, replacing only the allocation component. At equal or shorter wall-clock time, ALLOT outperforms every compared allocation strategy with XAttention, with an 11.8 dB PSNR gain on HunyuanVideo. Extensive experiments across four additional published pipelines on Wan2.1, Wan2.2, and HunyuanVideo show that ALLOT outperforms or ties the default in all nine settings.

AI.brief_summary: 提出免训练的块稀疏注意力分配方法 ALLOT：以 layer-step 为单元，通过 cell probing 与轨迹校准估计各单元对最终视频误差的贡献，并在实测时延预算下联合优化各单元密度，只替换分配组件而保留原有选择策略与 kernel。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「按层—步探测贡献 + 在资源预算下分配计算」的做法，可能为 LVR 中推理轨迹的贡献分配、动态计算与停止决策提供方法线索，但作者针对视频生成保真度，迁移性需核查。
